title: Hypothesis, Testability and Operationalization
purpose: Seed structured hypothesis formation and testability reasoning so Lantern can convert questions into evaluable claims, operationalize vague constructs, identify discriminating evidence and recognize when a proposed test cannot resolve the question.

concepts.definition: A sufficiently specified question identifying what is to be described, compared, explained, predicted or evaluated.
A proposed claim with enough structure to identify relevant evidence and possible outcomes that would support or challenge it.
A reference hypothesis used in some statistical testing frameworks, commonly representing no specified effect/difference; not the universal form of scientific skepticism.
A specified competing claim considered against another hypothesis.
Degree to which a claim can be connected to observations/evidence capable of differentiating it from relevant alternatives.
Whether possible observations could count against a claim under its stated assumptions/scope; useful but not the only criterion of scientific value.
A declared mapping from an abstract construct/question to observable/measurable variables or procedures.
A concept that may require operational definition before empirical measurement.
A variable treated as predictor/exposure/manipulated factor according to the design; the label alone does not establish causality.
An outcome/response variable measured or modeled in relation to predictors/conditions.
A variable held constant, adjusted for or otherwise accounted for according to a justified design.
A variable requiring causal/methodological consideration because it may distort the relationship of interest.
An expected observable result derived from a hypothesis under stated conditions.
An observation/result that would count substantially against a hypothesis under specified assumptions and adequate measurement.
A test whose possible outcomes differ meaningfully among competing hypotheses.
An additional assumption required to connect a hypothesis to a prediction/test; failures may implicate the assumption, measurement or hypothesis.
Recording hypotheses, outcomes and analysis decisions before observing the relevant test results to distinguish confirmatory from post-hoc reasoning.

guards.reason: A claim needs sufficient operational meaning before an empirical test can bear on it.
Immunity to contrary evidence is not confirmation.
An operational measure represents a construct under a method; it is not identical to the construct.
Variable labels/design roles alone do not establish causation.
Prediction may depend on auxiliary assumptions, measurement and scope.
A test cannot distinguish hypotheses when they predict the same observed result.
Hypotheses generated from data require fresh/held-out evidence for confirmatory testing.
Rejecting a statistical null does not automatically establish a specific substantive alternative.
Lack of current testability may reflect vague definitions, unavailable observations or technological limits; it is not itself falsity.
Testability is a methodological property, not a measure of significance or value.

invariants: A hypothesis should identify claim type, variables/constructs, scope, predictions and evidence that could challenge it where applicable.
Operational definitions are explicit mappings, not identities between constructs and measures.
Testability requires evidence that can bear differently on the hypothesis versus relevant alternatives.
A test that all competing hypotheses predict equally is not discriminating.
Independent/dependent variable labels do not establish causal direction.
Prediction failure can challenge a joint system of hypothesis, assumptions, measurement and scope; diagnosis precedes global rejection.
Hypotheses generated from observed data require fresh/held-out evidence before being treated as independently confirmed.
Not currently testable does not mean false.
Testability does not imply importance, truth or authority.
Structured hypotheses remain candidate epistemic objects until evidence updates their status.

provenance.authoring_basis: Scientific hypothesis formulation, falsifiability, operationalization and discriminating-test principles adapted to Lantern's typed scientific and causal architecture.
